articles.excerpt: Global music industry revenues are expected to reach approximately $200 billion annually by 2035 amid an improving outlook for subscription streaming. New subscription models, AI, and direct-to-consumer offerings are creating opportunities for the industry to reach audiences in new ways, according to Goldman Sachs Research. The music market undershot growth expectations over the last several years. The new forecast represents the first time in three years that Goldman Sachs Research has raised its long-term outlook for the industry, Stephen Laszczyk and Eric Sheridan write in the team’s 2026 edition of the annual “Music in the Air” report. Goldman Sachs Research expects global music revenues to increase at 6.7% year-on-year in 2026 and at a compound rate of 5.8% per year between 2025 and 2035. “While growth is likely to moderate from the pace observed during the industry's streaming adoption phase, we continue to see a long runway for industry expansion supported by favorable consumer behavior and an increasingly diversified monetization model,” Laszczyk and Sheridan write. Paid streaming subscriptions are helping to shore up the outlook for recorded music. After three consecutive downgrades to its forecast for 2030 recorded music revenues, Goldman Sachs Research’s outlook for the segment this year reflects improvements in streaming revenue, physical revenue, and download and other digital revenue. Subscription streaming revenue is growing faster, mainly because subscriber numbers are increasing more quickly than expected and revenue per user is rising in developed markets. articles.title: Emerging Market Credit Shows Resilience amid Energy Shock
articles.excerpt: When the Iran war triggered a surge in oil prices this year, many investors may have expected credit markets in the developing world to slide into a selloff. Instead, emerging market sovereign and corporate bonds weathered the shock with a newfound stability and solid performance for investors. The development is a key sign that emerging market credit is maturing into a resilient asset class, according to Anupam Damani, co-head and senior portfolio manager of emerging market debt at Goldman Sachs Asset Management. At the same time, investors are rethinking their approach to the market, which has trillions of dollars in outstanding debt. “Emerging market credit is now unrecognizable, and I mean that in a good way,” Damani says. “These bonds used to come with a crisis label, but this market is no longer monolithic. In my view, it has become a more diverse and resilient asset class, though risks remain.” To be sure, emerging market bonds run the gamut in terms of risk, and investors must be selective about what they trade in a marketplace with myriad issuers, she adds.

articles.title: The Rise of Healthcare Consumerism | Morgan Stanley
articles.excerpt: U.S. consumers are increasingly taking the lead in how they access and pay for healthcare, creating potential opportunities across biopharma and healthcare services. In the complex and costly U.S. healthcare system, patients are no longer just heeding drug ads to “Ask Your Doctor”—they’re going straight to the source. Policy changes and technological advances have given consumers more ways to directly choose the healthcare products and services that best suit their needs—including care, testing and medicines—as well as how they pay for them. The healthcare industry is adapting to this trend, potentially creating new opportunities for investors. In biopharma alone, the total direct-to-consumer cash-pay market could reach $26 billion at its peak. Eyeing that opportunity, many large-cap biopharma companies now offer direct-to-consumer platforms. Healthcare consumerism took root with the creation of Health Savings Accounts (HSAs) in 2003, followed by the growth of high-deductible health plans (HDHPs). These changes gave consumers more control over healthcare spending—but also shifted more of the costs and decisions to them.

articles.link_title: How AI Agents Could Disrupt Consumer Industries
articles.title: Winners and Losers From AI Agents | Morgan Stanley
articles.excerpt: As AI agents become more capable of making decisions and purchases on consumers’ behalf, Morgan Stanley Research examines which industries could benefit—and which face growing competitive pressure. The recent launch of powerful consumer AI agents has reignited debate over how artificial intelligence could disrupt industries ranging from retail and insurance to transportation and live entertainment. Unlike traditional AI tools that primarily answer questions, these agents can browse websites, complete forms, compare prices, make purchases and even help negotiate bills. Morgan Stanley Research estimates that roughly $30 trillion in consumer spending could be digitized through AI agents across online advertising, e-commerce, travel, food delivery, ridesharing, logistics, wearables and other sectors. The extent of the disruption will depend on how quickly consumers adopt AI agents and how effectively companies make money from agent-driven activity and transactions.

articles.excerpt: The AI buildout is accelerating, bringing binding constraints forward. We stay overweight U.S. equities and upgrade emerging market stocks to overweight but stay focused on opportunities driven by bottlenecks. Global government bond yields have surged through the summer. Higher yields have restored income opportunities, but only via a flexible approach. We prefer short-term bonds over long-term bonds with high sensitivity to interest rates. Asset-class buckets are a less useful starting point in a world shaped by mega forces. Infrastructure shows why: Its exposure to AI demand, energy security and fragmentation runs across markets and asset classes. The AI investment boom is having two broad impacts: lifting activity and earnings while absorbing more capital, power, materials and balance-sheet capacity. Heavy sovereign borrowing is adding to the demand for funding. The result is a higher cost of capital even as AI boosts growth. These developments reinforce our core Midyear Outlook themes: AI has the potential to deliver a sustained increase in growth and productivity, but that path to abundances runs through scarcity in capital, materials and labor.

Spreads on CCC-rated bonds have widened by more than 500 basis points from their lowest levels this year, to roughly 1,000 basis points over Treasuries. Meanwhile, spreads on higher-quality BB- and B-rated bonds have remained relatively contained. Because of their lower credit quality, CCC-rated bonds typically trade at a discount to the rest of high-yield. That discount is now larger than at any point since the COVID-19 market sell-off, raising investor concern about broader credit deterioration. The important question is whether the cracks at the bottom of the high-yield market are a signal for the broader credit market. A closer look at the Bloomberg U.S. Corporate High Yield Index suggests the picture is more nuanced: stress is concentrated, the market is higher quality than in the past, and attractive income opportunities remain. Four out of more than 150 CCC-rated issuers make up more than 30% of current CCC-rated bond spreads. Many of the companies most affected are in the telecommunications and media sector, where secular headwinds and company-specific challenges are driving distress. In other words, this has not been an indiscriminate repricing of credit risk. But that doesn’t mean investors should ignore it. Financial conditions have tightened this year. Interest rates on the broad U.S. bond market have increased by nearly 100 basis points, and this tightening is filtering through to parts of the credit market. Distress often appears first in the lowest-quality companies, which is not uncommon in the later stages of the credit cycle.

Roth IRAs offer tax-free growth and tax-free withdrawals in retirement, making them an attractive option for those who expect to be in a higher tax bracket in the future. Eligibility requirements for traditional and Roth IRAs differ primarily based on income levels and tax filing status. An emergency fund is an amount of money set aside in a dedicated savings account to help provide a financial safety net for life’s unexpected challenges. Common emergencies like unexpected medical bills, car troubles, or job loss can be overwhelming—but with an emergency fund, you can face these challenges with peace of mind. When is $2,000 as powerful as $1,000,000? Our research shows, $2,000 in an emergency fund can be just as powerful as having $1M in assets when it comes to your financial well-being. Think about it: If you’re lost in the desert and fighting heat and thirst, it only takes a small amount of water to keep you going. You could have all the water in the world back home, but you would get immediate relief from a much smaller amount that’s available right then and there. Your emergency fund is like water in the desert. Just $2,000 can give you a buffer against many of the things life can throw at you. Saving enough to cover at least half a month’s worth of living expenses can help you prepare for potential spending shocks. Income shocks are the unplanned loss of income. articles.link_title: A Systematic Lens On Global Equity Opportunities Within Multi Asset Portfolios
articles.title: A Systematic Lens on Global Equity Opportunities Within Multi-Asset Portfolios | PIMCO
categories: 投資戦略・資金フロー
articles.excerpt: Systematic equity investing is a way to invest in the stock market using clear rules and data, rather than guesswork or hunches. Instead of trying to pick stocks based on trends or headlines, this approach uses research, data, and technology to systematically identify opportunities across global markets. The goal? To help investors in PIMCO’s multi-asset strategies grow their investments more steadily, avoid over concentrations in big-name stocks, and help mitigate the volatility that often comes from following the “crowd”. Over the past several years, global equity markets have been defined by concentration, with a handful of mega-cap technology companies accounting for an outsized share of returns. This has led to a narrow bull market and pushed valuations higher, particularly in the U.S. Yet, as we enter 2026, the broad perception of “expensive equities” masks pockets of value and a growing opportunity set, supported by solid economic growth and improving earnings. For more than two decades, PIMCO has designed and managed global asset allocation strategies in which equities play a pivotal role. Within these multi-asset portfolios, equity exposures are implemented through a disciplined, data-driven and repeatable approach to pursuing equity alpha that is designed to help complement broader portfolio objectives rather than operate in isolation. In this context, we believe our systematic equity approach is well positioned for navigating toward more balanced and broader market participation. Our rules-based, systematic equity investment process focuses on identifying well-rounded companies across regions and sectors, helping our multi-asset portfolios remain broadly diversified while accessing sources of return potential that more traditional approaches may overlook.

articles.link_title: 5 Themes Defining Bond Etf Investing Today
articles.title: 5 Themes Defining Bond ETF Investing Today | PIMCO
articles.excerpt: Assessing both top-down macroeconomic and market-defining trends and bottom-up developments, flows, and risks, we’ve identified several key themes that characterize fixed income ETFs today and are likely to drive future opportunities. In the ever-evolving investment landscape, flexibility is becoming a watchword for fixed income investors. The surge in active core and multisector fixed income ETFs is evidence of this shift. Multisector ETFs – which barely registered two years ago – have ballooned recently, with over $20 billion in net inflows since mid-2023. Active core and core-plus ETF strategies now have more than $88 billion in assets, according to Morningstar. This rapid growth is not merely a function of product innovation, but a response to the demands of an uncertain market. The appeal is clear: In an environment marked by volatility and shifting macroeconomic signals, the agility of flexible, active strategies offers investors access to a broader opportunity set with the ability to pivot as conditions change. Elevated starting yields make fixed income attractive. Plus the negative correlation of fixed income – particularly short- to intermediate-maturity bonds – versus equity returns has reasserted itself, providing an important buffer against equity market drawdowns. As a result, active fixed income ETFs now account for nearly 40% of overall fixed income ETF flows, despite representing just 17% of total fixed income ETF assets, according to Bloomberg.

articles.excerpt: The European Central Bank (ECB) left its policy rate unchanged at 4% in December. As interest rates have presumably reached peak level, the focus has shifted towards when the ECB might start to cut. While recent inflation developments have been encouraging, the market is now fully pricing swift disinflation back to the central bank target, with the first rate cut around March next year. Although economic momentum in the euro area remains weak and recent inflation prints surprised to the downside, labour markets remain in good shape and the medium-term inflation trajectory uncertain. Underlying inflation is still at 3.6%, well above the 2% headline target. For inflation to evolve in line with ECB projections, growth in unit labour costs needs to falls back to levels consistent with 2% inflation, and firms need to use their profit margins as a buffer to limit the pass-through of the current strong wage increases to consumer prices. More clarity is needed for the ECB to change course. While the new staff macroeconomic projections include the inaugural estimates for 2026, the ECB has made clear that it aims to achieve its inflation target no later than in 2025. articles.link_title: Feds Dovish Pivot Reflects Lessons From History
articles.title: Fed’s Dovish Pivot Reflects Lessons From History | PIMCO
articles.excerpt: Following its December meeting, Federal Reserve officials underscored a growing confidence in their ability to guide the U.S. economy toward a soft landing, and therefore begin the process of cutting rates. As Fed Chair Jerome Powell himself stated in a 2018 speech, monetary policy strategy is an exercise in risk management. By softening the hiking bias embedded in previous Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) statements, and lowering the projected path of the federal funds rate, FOMC participants signaled they believe the balance of risks has shifted squarely in favor of achieving sustainably lower inflation. Thus, chances of further rate hikes have diminished, and FOMC discussion is quickly shifting toward the economic conditions that would warrant rate cuts. Because Chair Powell told reporters afterward that the FOMC had discussed the prospect of rate cuts at this meeting, markets have begun to focus on how soon and how many cuts could come. However, with the economy still proving resilient, Fed officials will likely want to hold off until additional evidence shows inflation is continuing to moderate back to the central bank’s 2% target. Still, history suggests that once the Fed does begin to cut, the pace could be more rapid than that implied by the FOMC’s projected median interest rate path through 2025. Both forecasters and markets have tended to underestimate the speed and magnitude of the central bank cutting cycle when rates are at their peak. The central bank held its policy rate steady at 5.25%–5.5%. It also released updated economic projections that we view as consistent with growing confidence that the U.S. economy will achieve a soft landing. articles.excerpt: 日前，施罗德投资《2026 全球投资者洞察调查》显示，在评估信贷投资机会时，近半数投资者（49%）会从整体投资组合角度出发，同步评估公开市场与非公开市场的信贷机会。 这也反映出投资者配置信贷资产的诉求早已不再局限于赚取收益。调查数据同时表明，市场不再将信贷视作单一资产品类，而是根据不同组合目标，匹配对应的信贷投资策略。 值得注意的是，施罗德投资的调查结果还清晰划分了不同信贷品类的核心功能——投资级信贷主要用于获取稳定收入；房地产债、基础设施债侧重增强组合韧性；高风险特色信贷策略则用于博取超额收益。 若以获取稳健真实收益为目标，投资者首选投资级企业债券。这一偏好源于全球金融危机、疫情超低利率周期结束后，固定收益市场经历重新定价。现阶段多数投资级企业债实际收益为正，可稳定贡献现金流。与此同时，即便宏观、地缘风险交织扰动，企业基本面依旧稳固，违约率维持低位，信贷质量未出现明显走弱。 此外，发达市场主权国债同样位列稳定真实收益的两大优选工具之一。一方面名义收益率较过往显著修复，另一方面部分市场发行通胀保值债券，可对冲实际现金流缩水风险。

articles.link_title: Equities Investors Portfolio Objectives Override Preferences For Private Or Public
articles.title: 施罗德投资：股票投资者的投资组合目标优
articles.excerpt: 施罗德投资发布的《2026 年全球投资者洞察调查》显示，投资者正逐渐从投资组合整体目标出发进行资产配置，相较于资产类别的结构性区别（如股票投资与私募股权），实现特定投资目标的重要性正变得更加突出。 本次调查访问了来自24个国家的1000多名专业投资者，结果显示，在全球经济和市场环境不确定性增加背景下， 85%的受访者预计未来一年市场波动将进一步加剧。因此，多元化配置（84%）以及下行风险防范和资本保值（83%）成为投资者最主要的投资目标，优先级均高于资本增长（37%）。 从数据看，投资者的资产配置思路正在发生转变，逐步突破传统资产类别划分的局限，转而从投资组合整体目标出发进行配置决策。当被问及如何看待公开市场股票和私募股权投资机会时，半数受访者表示他们采用统一的投资框架，综合评估公开市场和非公开市场的各类机会。在亚洲、中东和南美等地区，采取这一做法的投资者比例更高，达到53%至57%；而在欧洲、英国和美国，这一比例相对较低，为46%至49%。 对于长期资本增长，投资者青睐主动管理型仅做多公开市场股票策略、中小盘公开市场股票策略、大型企业私募股权投资策略和中小型私募股权策略。如图1所示，投资者对这些类别的偏好程度相近。同理，在寻求收益或抗通胀保护时，投资者对公开市场与非公开市场中的相关资产表现出大致相同的兴趣。 虽然投资者愿意在更广泛的资产范围内寻找投资机会，但他们在配置过程中依然会审慎评估各类资产的特征，以及其对投资组合可能带来的优势与挑战。当被问及公开市场与非公开市场之间的界限正在如何变化时，受访者普遍认识到私募股权所蕴含的投资机会具有潜在优势。其中，46%的受访者提到公司保持私有状态的时间越来越长。另有37%的受访者指出，机构资本正不断流入私募股权市场。与此同时，流动性问题仍受到投资者高度关注，47%的受访者表示，公开市场股票与私募股权之间的流动性差异"正变得更为重要"。
